title: Three squares per server start
plain: Instead of repeating all 24 build orders on two more squares one server restart at a time, each of the 24 runs builds all three squares far apart. That is 24 restarts, not 72.
why: Each restart costs about 20 seconds and 1 GB of the small memory, so the wider test fits in minutes.
done_when: The plan has exactly 24 server starts for 72 square runs, with every square's own order kept and the squares far apart.

title: Guess the best order from pairs
plain: Each pair of neighbour chunks may add or remove diamonds depending on which is built first. A small sum-of-pairs model is fitted from a few runs and predicts every other order.
why: Four chunks have 24 orders but nine have 362,880; the pair model needs about 37 runs for nine, so aiming scales past a square.
done_when: On a made-up table the model predicts unseen orders exactly, picks the best one, and says so when the table is not a sum of pairs.

title: Use the spawn area as it boots
plain: The server already builds a big area around the world spawn while it starts. The route is planned on that area, where a real run begins, with no extra build commands.
why: The fastest run starts at spawn, so planning there is both cheaper and the true starting map.
done_when: After a plain boot the reader finds a start square, a tree, stone and iron in the spawn area.

title: Numbers read live
plain: The page reads the experiment's result files when it opens instead of copying them in a build step. A missing file shows not run.
why: A copied number can go stale after a reset and look like a finding; a live read cannot.
done_when: With no result files every number says not run, and a changed file shows its new number at once.
